_why: A database or network lookup exception previously revoked a healthy phone and could tear down its desktop. Every physical frame still requires fresh account, desktop-device and bridge authorization. Failed checks deny the frame; explicit revocation and temporary authority unavailability have separate close semantics so reliable envelopes can resume without granting stale access.

threadTools.reason: Multiple valid logins for one account can replace the caller's device registration. Thread access must follow the authenticated account, not whichever login most recently registered that device.
threadTools.callerAddress: caller-provided return address, not an authenticated device identity
threadTools.reply: reauthorize the account and destination before returning a response or error

authorization.physicalFrameCheck: fresh before forwarding in both directions
authorization.failedCheck: deny frame and discard the peer physical queues without acknowledging logical delivery
authorization.retry: reauthorize on reconnect; preserve reliable message sequences and client message identities unchanged

diagnostics.pending: emit while a lookup is still pending
diagnostics.completion: emit duration after a slow lookup completes
diagnostics.sensitiveData: never include bearer tokens or backend exception messages

desktopRequestQuery.reason: App query scope belongs to the desktop API, while URL bearer/pairing credentials belong only to relay authentication.

heartbeat._why: Real WebSocket probes showed authorization queue high-water marks paused TCP reads, withholding automatic pongs despite healthy sockets. Application backlogs must not starve the WebSocket control plane.
heartbeat.controlFrames: continue reading ping/pong and close while application authorization is pending
heartbeat.downstreamBackpressure: mobile_ws_flow remains scoped to the destination phone
heartbeat.overload: retain hard peer frame/byte limits, global byte reservations, FIFO lanes and fair worker limits; close only the overloaded socket
